sample.title: Why More Americans Regret College And Homeownership
sample.description:
For generations, mortgages and student loans have been held up as textbook examples of “good debt,".This borrowing promises to  build wealth or increase your earning power over time. On the other side of the coin is so-called “bad debt”, things like auto loans or credit card debt that don’t provide a financial return over time. As the costs of buying a home and getting a degree have continued to climb, more Americans are questioning whether those “good debt” investments are actually paying off.

sample.title: Why There’s An ‘Extremely Fierce’ Battle For TSMC's Limited Chip Manufacturing Capacity
sample.description:
Unstoppable demand for AI is leading to a capacity crunch on factory lines at the world's leading chip manufacturer, Taiwan Semiconductor. And it could put a chokehold on AI's ability to scale. Analysts tell CNBC that Nvidia, Apple, Broadcom, AMD and others are locked in an “extremely fierce” competition to get their GPUs, CPUs and custom AI chips made at TSMC. Capacity can’t come online fast enough, despite TSMC’s rush to build new fabs in Taiwan, Japan and Arizona, where has expanded investment to $265 billion. The strain has made one man at TSMC “the most popular person on the planet,” as chip start-ups and big name CEOs visit Taiwan to ask him for wafer allocation. It’s also created a rich opportunity for Intel, as customers look to the long-struggling foundry arm of the U.S. chip manufacturer for a second source.

sample.title: Hundreds arrested in violent protests across France as buildings burned and looted | BBC News
sample.description:
There have been violent clashes between protesters and police in French cities, during the latest day of demonstrations against education standards and the cost of living.

At least 400 people were arrested during what the French government described as an "escalation in violence”, as more than 500,000 people took to the streets.

In Paris riot police used tear gas and water cannon on crowds. Buildings were set alight in the capital and other areas, including in Limoges where a large fire broke out in the town hall.

There was looting in several cities, with widespread vandalism against city halls and businesses. In Lyon the city’s tourist office was burned.  Police said "hostile individuals" prevented firefighters from tackling the blaze.

The interior ministry said the protests involved "targeted acts of violence" from "hooded individuals" in places, including parts of the capital and also Marseille, Rennes, Toulouse and Angers. Damage to buildings was reported across France, including in Grenoble, Avignon, Pau, Montpellier and Valence.

Hundreds of thousands of students have protested in recent weeks over staff shortages and dilapidated facilities in the country's lycées - secondary schools attended by 15 to 18-year-olds.  They were joined in the latest protests by trade union members and other protest groups. These included the so-called gilets jaunes 'yellow vest' movement, who demonstrated against cost-of-living hikes for over a year from 2018.

The protests come as Frances faces a period of deep political uncertainty.  President Emmanuel Macron will leave office next year and polls suggest April's presidential election could come down to a fight between the leader of the National Rally, Marine Le Pen, and Jean-Luc Mélenchon of the hard-left La France Insoumise party.

Jane Hill presents BBC News at Ten reporting by James Waterhouse and Katya Adler.
